purpose: Close the Japanese Marshall air baseline immediately before the Branch Flintlock-equivalent carrier approach, separating physical aircraft, combat-serviceable aircraft, search availability, named historical unit anchors and Branch-specific dispersal/readiness effects. v002 additionally decomposes a subset of fighter slots into Raiden and links base-defense C2 maturity without changing theater totals.
authority_note: No CURRENT authority promotion. Counts are working bands/centers, not a claim that every historical inventory source used the same definition of operational aircraft.

historical_anchors.official_US_Army: Eastern Mandates history reports about 110 operational Japanese aircraft in the Marshalls on 25 Jan 1944.
historical_anchors.NHHC: H-Gram 026 gives about 150 operational aircraft around 27 Jan; this conflicts in definition/rounding with the Army figure and is not treated as a like-for-like count.
historical_anchors.named_unit_compilation_29Jan: 252 AG fighters Taroa; 281 AG fighters Roi; 531 AG carrier-attack Wotje; 752 AG land-attack Roi/Taroa; 753 AG land-attack Roi; 952 AG recon seaplanes. Used for unit/location anchoring, not as an authoritative exact total.
historical_anchors.historical_search_effort: On 28 Jan historical Japanese search was very thin (about four daily search aircraft from Taroa in one major quadrant); Branch contact-fusion and healthier network permit somewhat more useful sorties, not blanket coverage.

branch_deltas: Historical Operation-RO 12-Nov drain is not inherited; the Branch Marshall network entered GALVANIC materially healthier.
GALVANIC caused real local land-air losses, including the 23-Nov torpedo strike, so the no-RO dividend is not retained one-for-one.
Historical mass 4-Dec Kwajalein/Roi carrier strike is not realized; only limited outer-Marshall pressure/recon occurred, preserving more aircraft/ground infrastructure into January.
Repeated Seventh Air Force attacks in Dec-Jan still impose losses, maintenance debt, runway repair and dispersal costs.
Branch C2/search doctrine favors dispersal, night staging, cue-to-confirm and preserving reconnaissance rather than parking the whole force at Roi.

theatre_total.warning: Physical, serviceable and immediately launchable are separate layers. Do not compare the 136 center directly to historical single-number sources without matching definitions.

base_layers.role_center: main eastern fighter/intercept base; 252 AG fighter core plus 752 AG attack detachment and search/confirmation assets
base_layers.branch_note: largest single forward air concentration, but kept below an all-network pile-up

useful outer-island staging; not a full independent fighter wing

base_layers.branch_note: detachment accounting only; no invented full named kokutai

base_layers.role_center: southern search/night staging and logistics node
western fallback/rear staging and land-attack reserve
base_layers.branch_note: rearward depth; not counted as instantly available over Kwajalein

search_contact_system.useful_long_range_search_sorties_per_day: 6-8 across the Marshall network under high alert
search_contact_system.fast_research_confirmation_sorties: 1-2 when a suspicious contact/submarine report exists
search_contact_system.effect: Submarine/DF/traffic reports narrow the arcs so limited aircraft can search probability corridors rather than the entire ocean.
limits: No airborne search radar assumed on these scouts.
US CAP/radar can break shadowing after the initial report.
A search contact is not a weapon-quality carrier strike solution without recontact/freshness.

kinsei_zero.dedicated_Marshall_combat_detachment_on_: 0 centered; 0-4 transient/evaluation aircraft possible but not credited
kinsei_zero.reason: Post-GALVANIC priority remains Shokaku/Zuikaku then Hiryu mixed groups; the already-adjudicated Bengal quality detachment consumes another small allocation. Do not spawn scarce Kinsei aircraft into every threatened shore base.
kinsei_zero.new_order_after_Central_Pacific_warning: 6-8 later-production aircraft may be ordered forward via Truk from 27-28 Jan, but ETA/acceptance is after this ledger clock and they are not counted on 28 Jan.

operational_conclusion: Branch Marshalls are materially harder to decapitate than the historical one-morning parking concentration. About 12-18 of the already-counted serviceable fighter slots can plausibly be Raiden detachments centered at Taroa/Roi, improving bomber/intermediate-altitude interception when warning survives. This does not create local air superiority over three US carrier groups, and scarce high-altitude Raiden are not enough to turn the network into a future B-29-proof defense.

raiden_composition_overlay.high_altitude_mechanical_supercharge_sub: 0-2 serviceable centered; scarce and not automatically pushed to outer islands
raiden_composition_overlay.accounting_guard: Subset of existing serviceable fighter/local-cover slots: no theater-total increase.
raiden_composition_overlay.identity_guard: Aircraft allocation overlay only; no untraced named-kokutai redesignation.

base_air_defense_c2_overlay.Taroa: A-/A-grade working node when radar/plot/radio intact; use Jan-28 post-GALVANIC exchange-transition band before suppression.
base_air_defense_c2_overlay.Roi: A-/B+ working node; high-value target and vulnerable to suppression, so maturity can fall rapidly after the first US strike.
base_air_defense_c2_overlay.outer_nodes: B/remote grade; useful warning and dispersal, not continuous precision fighter direction.
base_air_defense_c2_overlay.system_guard: No US-style continuous GCI. Radar/visual/DF/plot provides warning and coarse vectors; visual acquisition remains necessary.
